[SYSTEM] The OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (AIM) is a real-time tracking tool developed by the [OECD.AI Policy Observatory](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVUi7qVAjNNOTx69xH5ATui6ipL9aProgFmumHzx53OmaDa7NSpN5S9tM68o5UDj7Dr25w4-LXqdh1X88iNMFRJKVULlk3sQVOOpD7GUbOBA) in collaboration with the Patrick J. What is AIM?

* Real-Time Tracking: It continuously aggregates and analyzes world news using the Event Registry platform, processing over 150,000 news articles daily to detect AI-related events. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVsifMuhOaNwDAlzQjnIy4vrRKr8I29XG5C1WVNVzL3bhCTNw4fI2laOpcyKH7J9IvN8a-ZLn_J0sSyfVklrlhS5SXPO5ES6BEJry4oAExji4krUQwGXL-QXS8LA)]

[[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHrOzAVwqGhkYf9SorcbvbHFWp_yWUbilndOVejGwP1BWdb70lPllHnV1OjwaTm5Y9FgGTIZq7Kp8R6J_FH6eqmP3iFvVP96kVDPEpPu6PtUwb2-QUKtq1yM-9TeqGc3XFOXGl2Ii12XPQC4GTLKczY8Q)]
* Thematic Classification: Media reports are categorized into 14 distinct risk themes—including synthetic media, cyberattacks and fraud, autonomous vehicles, large language model (LLM) hallucinations, labour market disruptions, and child safety. d: THE OECD AIM, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a real-time tracking tool developed by the OECD.AI Policy Observatory in collaboration with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation'; it aggregates world news through Event Registry, 'processing over 150,000 news articles daily'; 14 risk themes; the definitions of incident and hazard. Six cards, five the OECD's own (the monitor, the methodology page, the May 2024 definitions report).
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview names the monitor's maker and supporter, says how it reads the news, sorts what it finds into themes, and defines its two kinds of event.
findings: THE PIPELINE'S INPUT RIGHT, ITS MACHINE UNSAID. Event Registry and the 150,000 articles a day are the methodology page's. That large language models have classified the events since November 2024 and written their titles and summaries (GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, o3-mini) is not said. The record reads the monitor as itself a machine reception of the news; the composition reads it as an aggregator of the news. Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.

THE MAKER. The methodology page says the monitor 'was initiated and is being developed by the OECD.AI expert group on AI incidents' with support from the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation; 'developed by the OECD.AI Policy Observatory in collaboration with' is close.
FOURTEEN THEMES. The count comes from a card ('Trends in AI incidents and hazards reported by the media'); the methodology page read gives no count of themes. Not verified here.
analysis: The monitor is composed from its own methodology page with its inputs and definitions right and its classifier left out, the part of its method that makes each record a machine composition. The record holds what the composition drops.
per_note: OECD.AI and the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation named; no person; the OECD's own pages cited.
